payload.swept:
One describing surface taught the superseded lane and was rewritten; the rest are self-documenting or already correct.

se.guidance-worktrees - REWRITTEN. It previously taught only 'merge at ship, trunk untouched until then', which is now less than half the story. It gains: milestone commits landing on the iteration's own branch; the close as a SPLIT with live claims to trunk and events left on the branch; the tag as mandatory AND first, because the record must be named before any of it leaves the tree; the refusal rule, that an empty branch, an untaggable close and a conflict all leave trunk unchanged; the toolchain being installed rather than linked, pointing at the read-only import law; and the grant index staying on trunk as what keeps a closed iteration listable. Its statement was updated to match.

THE ONE THAT MATTERS TO THE OWNER, and the reason this sweep is not cosmetic: PUSH WITH TAGS is now a rule in that guidance. Git does not push tags by default, and after this iteration the tag is the ONLY handle on an iteration's record - a plain `git push` would ship the live claims with nothing behind them, and a clone would find every evidence pointer dangling. The guidance names --follow-tags, and forbids shallow clones (--depth) while noting --filter=blob:none is safe. This is also carried as se.raid-tags-not-pushed with the owner as its owner, because the owner performs every push.

Surfaces checked and NOT changed, with reasons: the ADRs and the new law carry their own why and are the durable home for it, so nothing restates them at the application sites; se_loop_start's description already says every iteration opens in its own worktree, which is unchanged; guidance-phone-setup is untouched by this iteration. No surface now teaches the old close.
